lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Saturday, 9 a.m., the community club under Block 208. Concert tonight.
**Mr Tan:** Kavya! A dancer in Priya's item has sprained her ankle. Congratulations. You're in.
**Kavya:** Mr Tan, I don't dance. I do maths.
**Priya:** Same thing! Every dance is three moves: **slide**, **flip** and **turn**. I'll teach you by lunch.
**Dad:** And I'm on lights, projector and the banner ladder. Leave it to me. **Nailed it.**
**Ah Boy:** And I'm doing a shadow-puppet dinosaur! It's going to be **ENORMOUS**!
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the tall mirror in the rehearsal room.
**Madame Miroir:** Madame Miroir. The **mirror**. Thirty years in this room. I have seen every **wrong move**.
**Kavya:** So when I raise my **right** hand...
**Madame Miroir:** ...in me, it is your **left**. A reflection **reverses** everything. Nothing personal.
**Ah Boy:** Madame, why is your name written backwards?
**Madame Miroir:** It is not backwards. **You** are backwards.
**Narrator:** Slide, Flip, Turn. Episode 17: Three Right, Two Down.
**Narrator:** Ten hours to showtime. Mum is painting the backdrop: a wall of **Peranakan tiles**.
**Mum:** Each tile must match whichever way round it goes. Kavya, how symmetrical is it?
**Kavya:** Up, across, and both diagonals. **Four** lines of symmetry.
**Twirla:** Twirla! **Rotational symmetry**! Turn it about its centre: it fits its outline **four** times in one turn. **Order 4**!
**Ah Boy:** The banner's a rectangle, so four lines too. But folded on the diagonal it's a sad envelope.
**Kavya:** A **rectangle** has only **2** lines. A **square** has 4. And a rectangle fits after a half-turn: **order 2**.
**Dad:** This **parallelogram** tile has no lines of symmetry. So its order is **zero**. Nailed it.
**Twirla:** Everything fits **once** per turn, so **no** rotational symmetry is **order 1**. This one fits after a half-turn: **order 2**.
**Mum:** Centrepiece: a **regular hexagon**, like a snowflake.
**Kavya:** A regular polygon with **n** sides: **n** lines, order **n**. Hexagon: **6** and **6**.
**Twirla:** Smallest turn that works: **360° ÷ n**. For the hexagon, 360 ÷ 6 = **60°**.
**Mr Tan:** Backwards: a hubcap's smallest turn is **40°**. Order: 360 ÷ 40 = **9**. That's how I roll.
**Narrator:** 10 a.m. The stage. Priya has taped a **grid** on the floor. Every dancer has a mark.
**Priya:** We start in a triangle. Me at **(1, 3)**, Kavya at **(3, 3)**, Ah Boy at **(1, 5)**.
**Vic:** Vic. Stage manager. **Column vector**. I call every move. First call: **5 over −2**!
**Ah Boy:** Top number is up! So **5 up**, then two... sideways?
**Vic:** No! **Top: across**, right is plus. **Bottom: up or down.** Along the corridor, then up the stairs.
**Kavya:** So **5 right**, **2 down**: add 5 to every x, take 2 from every y.
**Vic:** A **translation**: every point slides the same distance, same direction. Same size, same way round: **congruent**.
**Dad:** Spotlight: from **(4, −1)** to Kavya at **(−2, 3)**. 6 right, 4 up. Nailed it.
**Kavya:** **Image minus object.** Across: −2 − 4 = **−6**, that's 6 **left**. Up: 3 − (−1) = **4**. So **−6 over 4**.
**Mr Tan:** Lovely. Now please move it **back** off my face.
**Vic:** To undo a translation, change **both** signs: **6 over −4**.
**Priya:** Big finish: Ah Boy slides **2 over 5**, then **−7 over −1**.
**Kavya:** One move does both. Add the tops: **−5**. Add the bottoms: **4**. **−5 over 4**.
**Narrator:** 11 a.m. The rehearsal room. The **mirror section**.
**Priya:** Half of us are the **mirror images** of the other half, across the line **x = 4**.
**Madame Miroir:** My section. **Same distance. Other side. At right angles.**
**Kavya:** Ah Boy at **(1, 1)** is **3** squares left of x = 4, so his twin is 3 right: **(7, 1)**.
**Madame Miroir:** **(3, 1)** → **(5, 1)**. **(1, 4)** → **(7, 4)**. Same y. And the shape is **reversed**.
**Dad:** Second song: mirror line **y = 3**. It goes through 3 on the y-axis, so it's **vertical**. Nailed it.
**Madame Miroir:** Every point on **y = 3** has y-coordinate 3. It lies **flat**. **y = b lies down; x = a stands up.**
**Priya:** Finale: the mirror is the diagonal, **y = x**. Ah Boy, you're at **(3, 1)**.
**Ah Boy:** I counted straight across: two to the line, two more. x = −1, y = 1: **(−1, 1)**!
**Madame Miroir:** At **right angles** to me, child! Or simply **swap** the coordinates: (3, 1) becomes **(1, 3)**.
**Kavya:** And for **y = −x**: swap, then change **both** signs. (1, 2) goes to **(−2, −1)**.
**Mr Tan:** Puzzle. (2, 5) lands on (2, −1), and (6, 4) on (6, 0). Where's the mirror?
**Kavya:** **Midpoints**: (2, 2) and (6, 2). Both have y = 2. The mirror is **y = 2**.
**Ah Boy:** Madame, why is **AMBULANCE** written backwards on ambulances?
**Madame Miroir:** So drivers can read it in their mirror. At last, somebody writes for **me**.
**Narrator:** Noon. Seven hours to go. Time for the big **turn**.
**Priya:** On the drum beat, everybody **rotate 90°**!
**Ah Boy:** I'm rotating! I'm rotating!
**Twirla:** Stop! Rotate about **what**? Which **way**? I don't spin without **CAD**: **C**entre, **A**ngle, **D**irection.
**Twirla:** Every point keeps its distance from the **centre**, so you usually end up somewhere **else**.
**Priya:** Fine: **90° anticlockwise** about the **origin**. Tracing paper says it lands here.
**Dad:** For the encore: **clockwise**. That's this way. Nailed it.
**Kavya:** Dad, **clockwise** is the way the **clock hands** move. And 90° clockwise is the same as 270° anticlockwise.
**Twirla:** **90° clockwise**: (x, y) → **(y, −x)**. **180°**: (x, y) → **(−x, −y)**. A half-turn needs no direction.
**Priya:** Me at **(5, 2)**: **90° clockwise** about Kavya at **(2, 1)**.
**Kavya:** Step from the centre: **3 across, 1 up**. Turned clockwise: **1 across, 3 down**. Add it on: **(3, −2)**.
**Mr Tan:** A **half-turn** sends (1, 2) to (5, 4). Where's the centre?
**Ah Boy:** I've been spinning since the drum beat. Which way is the floor?
**Narrator:** 2 p.m. Ah Boy's shadow-puppet dinosaur. Dad is on the projector.
**Ah Boy:** My dinosaur is only **5 cm** tall. I want it **ENORMOUS**!
**Mr Zoom:** Mr Zoom. Overhead projector, 1987. I **enlarge**. My lamp is the **centre of enlargement**.
**Mr Zoom:** Light goes in straight lines from me. Puppet **20 cm** away, screen **60 cm**: 60 ÷ 20 = **scale factor 3**.
**Kavya:** So the shadow is 3 × 5 = **15 cm** tall. Every length × 3; the **angles** stay the same. **Similar**.
**Priya:** Now the poster. Enlarge this triangle by **scale factor 2**, centre **(1, 1)**.
**Dad:** Easy. I start at the **edge** of the triangle and double from there. Nailed it.
**Mr Zoom:** From the **centre**, always! (1, 1) to (3, 2): **2 across, 1 up**. Doubled: **4 across, 2 up**. Land on **(5, 3)**.
**Kavya:** (5, 2): 4 across, 1 up, doubled: **(9, 3)**. (3, 4): 2 across, 3 up, doubled: **(5, 7)**.
**Mum:** Costume: a **2 cm by 3 cm** sequin patch, scale factor **4**. So I bought four times the sequins.
**Kavya:** Lengths × 4: **8 by 12**. Perimeter 10 → **40**: × 4. But area 6 → **96 cm²**: × **16**.
**Mr Zoom:** Area × 4². So scale factor 2? Area **× 4**, not double.
**Mum:** Sixteen packets of sequins. I bought four.
**Kavya:** Small dinosaur to big: base 1 became 3, so **scale factor 3**. Then **ray lines** through matching corners...
**Mr Zoom:** ...meet at the centre: **(0, 1)**. Image ÷ object for the scale factor; ray lines for the centre.
**Narrator:** 5 p.m. Dress rehearsal. Mr Tan runs a quiz: **Name That Move**.
**Auntie Rose:** Auntie Rose, guest judge. I brought kueh. Describe **fully** the **single** transformation, okay?
**Mr Tan:** First: shape **A** to shape **B**.
**Priya:** It **moved**.
**Vic:** Same size, facing the same way, just slid: a **translation**. Give me the **vector**.
**Kavya:** (1, 1) went to (−5, 3). Across −6, up 2. **Translation by −6 over 2**.
**Priya:** A to **C** is flipped: (1, 1) ↔ (1, −1). **Reflection** in the **x-axis**: the line **y = 0**.
**Dad:** A to **D**: **rotation, 180°**. Nailed it.
**Twirla:** About **where**, darling? (1, 1) → (−1, −1): midpoint **(0, 0)**. **Rotation 180° about (0, 0)**.
**Kavya:** **Rotations need CAD; enlargements need SC.** Reflections need the mirror line's **equation**.
**Auntie Rose:** So which ones are **congruent**, ah?
**Kavya:** Translate, reflect, rotate: **congruent**, same shape **and** size. Enlargements: **similar**, same angles, sides in the same ratio.
**Ah Boy:** So **congruent** is twins. And **similar** is... me and Dad.
**Auntie Rose:** Ten out of ten! Everybody have a kueh. Priya, have two. You **moved**.
**Narrator:** 6 p.m. One hour to go. The banner is still on the floor.
**Dad:** The ladder is **6.5 m** long, and its foot is **2.5 m** from the wall. How high does it reach?
**Hypo:** Hypo. The **hypotenuse**: the longest side, opposite the **right angle**. Also, today, a ladder.
**Kavya:** The wall and the floor make the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: **a² + b² = c²**.
**Hypo:** You **added**? Adding gives the **hypotenuse**: me. **Longest side? Add. Shorter side? Subtract.**
**Priya:** My grand leap: corner to corner across the stage, **7 m** by **15 m**.
**Kavya:** Hypotenuse, so **add**: d² = 7² + 15² = 49 + 225 = **274**.
**Priya:** So I leap **274 metres**?!
**Mum:** Builders check corners with **3 m**, **4 m**, **5 m**: 3² + 4² = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5².
**Kavya:** A **Pythagorean triple**! So are **5, 12, 13** and **6, 8, 10**. Only in **right-angled** triangles.
**Ah Boy:** I'm the shortest side. I'm fine with it.

chapters.title: The cast saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the curtain goes up, the cast would like to save you some marks.
**Twirla:** One. Never write just '**rotation**'. Give the **centre**, the **angle** and the **direction**.
**Mr Tan:** Two. '**Single** transformation' means **one**. Not 'reflect, then translate'.
**Dad:** Three. The line **x = a** stands up. **y = b** lies down. Ask me how I know.
**Vic:** Four. **Top** number across, **bottom** number up or down. And never lose the **minus** sign.
**Mr Zoom:** Five. Measure an enlargement from the **centre**, not from the edge of the shape.
**Hypo:** Six. Don't stop at **c²**. **Square-root** it.
**Narrator:** Slide, Flip, Turn will return.
**Priya:** Item seven! Five, six, seven, eight: **slide**, **flip**, **turn**!
**Dad:** Lights on. Projector on. Banner up. **Nailed it.**
**Madame Miroir:** Bravo, Kavya. You were all **perfect**.
**Kavya:** Really?
**Madame Miroir:** No. I **reverse** everything.
